correctness.rationale: Alternating R-bilinearity gives [X,Y]=(ad−bc)e even in characteristic two, and each further bracket with X multiplies by a. For fixed X the image is a^{m−1}(a,b)R, with valuation s=min(ell,(m−1)nu(a)+min(nu(a),nu(b))) for a≠0, while a=0 gives zero for m≥2. Counting first inputs gives M_s, and a target in that ideal has exactly q^{ell+s} preimages of the additive map. At each positive valuation below ell the increment is precisely M_s q^{ell+s} and is nonzero exactly on the stated union of integer intervals. Zero adds a strict final level since a=0 always contributes. For m≥ell+1 all nonunit a yield the zero operator, while for 2≤m≤ell the choice nu(a)=1, nu(b)=0 gives a proper nonzero image. This proves the cutoff and the stable formulas, including ell=1 when all stipulated depths are stable.
residual_risks: Bounded enumeration is corroboration only; the valuation and kernel-size argument applies to all finite commutative chain rings. The claim excludes depth one and non-chain rings.

value.rationale: This is an exact and interpretable distribution for a natural word on the basic nonabelian split solvable Lie algebra over chain rings. It explains why prescribed-target counts agree across different ramification and exhibits exactly where frequencies change, including the sharp transition to flat nonzero fibers. This is more than the routine observation that a fixed-X linear map has fibers of equal size on its image.
residual_risks: No claim about general Lie rings, non-chain local rings, or group Engel words is supported by this calculation.
